subject: Embeddings model fit validation — next steps and eval artifacts
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Cho <sara.cho@atlassearch.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Embeddings evaluation — recap & next steps

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the call today — really appreciated the context on the product search use case and the examples you shared. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Recap:
- Goal: improve semantic ranking for product search across SKU/title/description with expected latency <= 35ms p99 and storage/cost constraints for ~10M vectors.
- Current infra: Elastic + ANN index (Milvus) with 768-d embeddings, nightly re-index.
- Primary success metrics: recall@10, MRR, and precision@5 for top-k relevance. Secondary: inference cost per 1k queries, index size, and embedding drift week-over-week.

Proposed next steps for model-fit evaluation:
1) You share a sample of ~5k-20k queries + expected relevance (or click labels). A CSV like the one attached works.
2) We run a controlled eval locally against a couple model candidates and provide a benchmark deck: recall@1/5/10, MRR, mean cosine distance, and latency/cost estimates.
3) If results look promising, we run a larger, production-like sweep and provide a recommended model/profile to deploy (plus quantization suggestions).

Model recommendations to test (initial):
- redwood-embed-small-v1 (768 dim) — low-cost baseline, good for throughput.
- redwood-embed-large-v2-quant (1024 dim, 8-bit quant) — higher-quality, lower storage with quantization tradeoffs.

Evaluation notes / what we'll measure:
- Metrics: recall@10, MRR, map@k, cosine vs dot-product scoring; p99 latency (embedding generation) for typical batch sizes; index size and storage estimates.
- Dimensionality tradeoff: 768 vs 1024 — higher dims may improve MRR but increase index memory and cost.
- Drift monitoring: we'll compute weekly centroid shift and distribution distance (KL / Wasserstein on embedding norms) and set an alert if week-over-week MRR drops >5% or centroid shift > threshold.
- Quality regression guardrails: we recommend a candidate be rejected if it degrades recall@10 by >=5% or MRR by >=3% compared to baseline.

Attachments: I attached a small sample template (atlas_search_sample_queries.csv). If you can drop a sample (or an S3 link) we'll kick off an initial run.

Links we'll share once we run the eval: a Drive notebook with results + a short benchmark deck (we'll include recommended prompt sets for any semantic re-ranking steps).

Would you be able to share a sample dataset and confirm whether 768-d embeddings are the current production dimensionality? Also, any constraints on generating embeddings at request-time vs offline?

Thanks — we can run an initial benchmark this week once we have the sample.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Sara Cho <sara.cho@atlassearch.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:14:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Embeddings evaluation — recap & next steps

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the clear recap. A few quick notes:
- Confirmed: current production embeddings are 768-d and generated offline nightly. We'd be interested in seeing the 1024-d/quantized tradeoffs but storage is a primary concern.
- Dataset: I can share ~10k labeled queries (click labels + relevance buckets). I uploaded a sample to our S3: s3://atlassearch-eval/sample-queries/2027-08-30.csv (public-read link attached).
- Latency: our target is <50ms end-to-end for user-facing search; p99 embedding generation can be higher if we cache, but index lookup must be fast.

Questions: 
1) For the 8-bit quantized variant, what loss in MRR have you typically observed vs full-precision?
2) Do you simulate index-level tradeoffs (e.g., HNSW ef/search params) as part of the eval?

I attached a small sample CSV (same structure as your template) — let me know if the S3 link works. Happy to set up a short session with our infra lead if you need deeper access.

Thanks,
Sara
Head of Search — AtlasSearch
+1 (646) 555-3310

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Cho <sara.cho@atlassearch.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 11:02:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Embeddings evaluation — recap & next steps

Sara — great, thanks for the sample and context. The S3 link works for us.

Short answers to your questions:
1) Quantization impact: in our internal benchmarks we typically observe a 1-4% MRR delta for 8-bit quantization on large models (varies by dataset). For some product-search distributions the hit can be <1% when paired with re-ranking. We'll report exact deltas for your data.
2) Index-level simulation: yes — we'll run HNSW parameter sweeps (efConstruction / efSearch) and simulate recall vs latency tradeoffs to recommend index params alongside the embedding model.

Plan & deliverables: 
- Rishi will run an initial 10k evaluation pass this week using two candidates (redwood-embed-small-v1, redwood-embed-large-v2-quant). He'll produce: recall@1/5/10, MRR, mean cosine similarity, embedding norm distributions, p50/p95/p99 embed latency, and estimated index size.
- Deliver a short benchmark notebook (Drive link below) and a one-page recommendation with suggested model + index params.
- If candidate meets guardrails, we'll propose a pilot on a subset of production traffic.

Attached: embedding_eval_notebook.ipynb (runnable notebook) and evaluation_prompt_set.json (the prompt sets and eval script config).

Quote of your note for context:
> From: Sara Cho <sara.cho@atlassearch.com>
> Confirmed: current production embeddings are 768-d and generated offline nightly. We'd be interested in seeing the 1024-d/quantized tradeoffs but storage is a primary concern.

We'll start the runs and circle back with preliminary results by end of week. If you want deeper infra access, CC your infra lead and we'll coordinate.

Thanks —
Marcus (on behalf of Rishi)
